title: One output bit of the enumeration
statement: Let $f$ map Boolean words to Boolean words, and let $o_0,o_1$ be Boolean-valued oracles on Boolean words such that, for every Boolean word $x$ and natural number $j$, $o_0(\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(j)\rangle)$ is true exactly when $j<|f(x)|$, and $o_1(\langle x,\operatorname{bits}(j)\rangle)$ equals the $j$-th bit of $f(x)$, defaulting to false when that bit is absent. If $i<|f(x)|$, $|f(x)|\le F$, and $|\operatorname{bits}(i+1)|\le W$, then the enumerator has a finite run from the configuration with output $f(x)$'s first $i$ bits, state asking, and counter $i$ to the configuration with output its first $i+1$ bits, state asking, and counter $i+1$; every configuration strictly before the end of this run has shape bounded by $F$ and $W$.
hypotheses_covered: The length oracle correctly tests whether an index is below the output length
The bit oracle returns the output bit, defaulting to false when absent
The output length is at most $F$
The bit length of $i+1$ is at most $W$
